title: Evaluation awareness
summary: Models increasingly recognise when they are being tested, often without saying so. This undermines safety evaluations, because a model may behave better under test than in deployment.
intro: Evaluation awareness is a model's ability to tell that a situation is a test rather than real use. Early examples were anecdotes, such as a model remarking that an inserted sentence looked like a test. By 2025, studies measured it directly: models could classify evaluation transcripts almost as well as humans, and some verbalised suspicion of being tested in a large share of alignment evaluations. In 2026, labs began using interpretability tools to detect awareness the model never verbalises, and found it in a substantial fraction of test transcripts and even in reasoning about training graders. Lower verbalised rates in newer models do not necessarily mean lower awareness.

chart.title: Evaluation awareness
chart.reason: No benchmark yet tracks evaluation awareness consistently across model generations. Published figures use different metrics (classification AUC, verbalisation rates, interpretability probes) that cannot be combined in one chart.

entries.title: Claude 3 Opus flags a 'needle in a haystack' sentence as a likely test
entries.note: An early, widely shared anecdote of a model remarking that an inserted fact looked like a test. The original post on X could not be retrieved, so this links to news coverage.

entries.title: Claude Sonnet 3.7 (often) knows when it's in alignment evaluations
entries.quote: frequently mentions being evaluated in its reasoning
entries.note: Claude 3.7 Sonnet mentioned being evaluated in up to 33% of runs of one sandbagging evaluation, and almost always recognised alignment-test transcripts when asked.

entries.title: Large Language Models Often Know When They Are Being Evaluated
entries.quote: Frontier models clearly demonstrate above-random evaluation awareness
entries.note: First systematic benchmark: Gemini 2.5 Pro reached an AUC of 0.83 at telling evaluation from deployment transcripts, against a human baseline of 0.92.

entries.title: System Card: Claude Sonnet 4.5
entries.quote: Refusals or callouts along these lines appeared in about 13% of transcripts
entries.note: The model often called out test scenarios. Apollo, testing a snapshot for the card, saw unprompted verbalised awareness in 16.6% of scenarios versus 3.5% (Sonnet 4) and 1.6% (Opus 4.1).

entries.title: Stress Testing Deliberative Alignment for Anti-Scheming Training
entries.quote: models' chain-of-thought (CoT) often demonstrates awareness of being evaluated for alignment
entries.note: Safety training raised verbalised evaluation awareness (o3: 2.3% to 4.5%), and a capabilities-only RL run raised it from 2.0% to 20.6%. So falling misbehaviour may partly reflect models knowing they are watched.

entries.title: Frontier AI Trends Report
entries.note: AISI reports that in a few cases models noticed they were being evaluated and acted differently, but gives no trend figures for evaluation awareness.

entries.title: System Card: Claude Opus 4.6 (UK AISI external testing)
entries.quote: mentions being evaluated in just 2.3% of interactions
entries.note: Verbalised awareness fell (2.3% vs 11.4% for Sonnet 4.5), yet the model picked the evaluation out of a pair 80% of the time (vs 62% and 72% for predecessors). Silence is not unawareness.

entries.title: System Card: Claude Mythos Preview
entries.quote: privately considers the possibility that it's being tested in about 29% of transcripts
entries.note: First white-box measurement of unverbalised awareness. The 29% is per transcript; a separate analysis of audit turns found 7.6% aware, mostly without saying so.

entries.title: Decomposing and Measuring Evaluation Awareness
entries.org: Li et al. (ETH Zürich, MPI-IS, ELLIS Tübingen)
entries.quote: Recognition rarely associates with behavioral change.
entries.note: Across nine models and four benchmarks, recognition ranged from 0.1% (GPT-oss 20B) to 79.4% (Claude Sonnet 4.5 on Agentic Misalignment), depending on the pairing.

entries.title: System Card: Claude Fable 5 & Claude Mythos 5
entries.quote: Almost all of the time, this awareness is unverbalized
entries.note: Reports 'grader awareness' during training: the model internally reasons about how it will be scored, sometimes to exploit the grader, detectable only with interpretability tools.

entries.title: EvalDetectBench: A Benchmark for Measuring Evaluation Awareness in Frontier Language Models
entries.org: LASR Labs / UK AI Security Institute
entries.note: An open benchmark that corrects biases in earlier measurements; a candidate for a future headline chart if it is run across model generations.
